headline: Westlake Robotics, a Chinese company, says its new WR1 control system lets two humanoid robots fold a pair of trousers together with dexterous hands, which it calls a world first.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a striking demonstration, but it is the company's own video, unverified, and the footage dates from 9 October.
importance_line: It points to humanoid robots getting closer to soft household items such as laundry, which could matter for home and factory work one day, but it is a company demonstration, the world-first claim is unverified and no success rate is given.
summary: Pandaily reports that Westlake Robotics, a Hangzhou company spun out of Westlake University, released WR1, a general control "brain" for humanoid robots that plans walking, posture and hand movement as one action sequence, and showed in footage published on 9 October a humanoid doing a kitchen-to-bedroom chore run and two robots passing, spreading and folding trousers. The company says no humanoid had publicly folded a whole garment with dexterous hands before, a claim no one else has checked.
